Summarise Multi-State Occupation Probabilities over time

Source: R/summariseMultiStateProbabilities.R
summariseMultistateProbabilities.Rd

Prepare state transitions with prepareMultistateData(), estimate state occupation probabilities, and return a standard summarised_result for inspection or plotting with plotMultistateProbabilities().

Usage

summariseMultistateProbabilities(
  cohort,
  trans,
  strata = list(),
  followUpDays = Inf,
  eventDate = "cohort_start_date",
  censorDate = NULL,
  stateHierarchy = character(),
  stateStep = 0.01
)

Arguments

cohort

A cohort_table object containing one cohort for each state in the multi-state model. Cohort names must match the state names in trans.

trans

Transition matrix describing the states and transitions in the multi-state model. If S is the number of states in the multi-state model, trans should be an S x S matrix, with (i,j)-element a positive integer if a transition from i to j is possible in the multi-state model, NA otherwise. In particular, all diagonal elements should be NA. The integers indicating the possible transitions in the multi-state model should be sequentially numbered, 1,...,K, with K the number of transitions. Row and column names must be identical, unique state names in the same order. A row containing only NA defines an absorbing state. Use transMat() to build a matrix.

strata

List of character vectors defining stratifications. Each character vector identifies one or more columns in cohort; a separate model is fitted for each combination of values. For example, list("sex", c("sex", "age_group")) requests models by sex and by sex and age group jointly. An unstratified model is always included. Each column must be constant within a person across all cohort records. Missing values are labelled "Missing".

followUpDays

Maximum number of days of follow-up for which to estimate state occupation probabilities. Use Inf to include all available follow-up. This limits the time points returned after model fitting; it does not censor the input data or refit the model at this horizon.

eventDate

Name of the date column in cohort that identifies when an individual enters a state. State entries are defined by these dates; reaching cohort_end_date does not automatically create a state change.

censorDate

Name of the date column in cohort that identifies the end of follow-up, inclusive. If NULL, the end of each individual's observation period is used. Missing values in a supplied column also fall back to the observation period end. Supplied dates replace the observation-based dates; they are not automatically capped at observation end. Use the same date on all state records for a person when specifying a single follow-up endpoint.

stateHierarchy

Character vector of state names in the order used to resolve states that occur on the same date, with earlier entries occurring first. An empty character vector applies no hierarchy; unresolved ties between competing states cause an error. Include all states that need a distinct order. Unlisted states share the priority of the last listed state.

stateStep

Numeric increment used to separate states that occur on the same date according to stateHierarchy, in days. Successive priority ranks are shifted by multiples of this increment. The default is 0.01 days.

Value

A summarised_result with result type "summarise_multistate_probabilities". Use tidy() to obtain columns:

  • initial_state: the conditioning state, or "overall" for the weighted estimate;

  • variable_name: "prob_" followed by the destination state name;

  • variable_level: elapsed days since time zero, stored as character;

  • probability: state occupation probability on a scale from zero to one;

  • requested strata columns, with "overall" for unstratified results.

settings() contains analysis settings, including the permitted transitions and follow-up horizon. The ms_data attribute contains the prepared data used for fitting, with any requested strata columns.

Details

Each model uses survival::coxph() with a separate baseline hazard for each transition, clustering by person, and Breslow handling of tied event times. mstate::msfit() and mstate::probtrans() then estimate state occupation probabilities from time zero. Time zero, censoring, and exclusions follow prepareMultistateData().

Results are provided conditional on each initial state, together with an overall estimate weighted by the observed distribution of initial states in that model's population. When strata are requested, this is repeated within each stratum, alongside the unstratified analysis. If fitting fails for a stratum, an informational message identifies it and the underlying error; that stratum contributes no probability rows.

Time points are those returned by the fitted model, including time zero, restricted to followUpDays. A row at exactly followUpDays is not guaranteed. Confidence intervals are not included in the returned result.

See also

prepareMultistateData(), plotMultistateProbabilities(), filterGroup(), filterStrata()

Examples

library(CohortConstructor)
library(dplyr)
library(omock)
library(OmopMultistate)

cdm <- mockCdmFromDataset(datasetName = "GiBleed")
#> ℹ Loading bundled GiBleed tables from package data.
#> ℹ Adding drug_strength table.
#> ℹ Creating local <cdm_reference> object.

# An illustrative concept set: aspirin 81 mg oral tablets.
# Keep the first treatment episode for each person.
cdm$treated <- conceptCohort(
  cdm = cdm,
  conceptSet = list(treated = 19059056L),
  name = "treated"
) |>
  requireIsFirstEntry()
#> ℹ Subsetting table drug_exposure using 1 concept with domain: drug.
#> ℹ Combining tables.
#> ℹ Creating cohort attributes.
#> ℹ Applying cohort requirements.
#> ℹ Merging overlapping records.
#> ✔ Cohort treated created.

# Enter the untreated state the day after treatment ends. Require that day
# to be within observation, so loss to follow-up is not a discontinuation.
cdm$untreated <- cdm$treated |>
  padCohortEnd(days = 1L, requireFullContribution = TRUE, name = "untreated") |>
  padCohortDate(
    days = 0L,
    indexDate = "cohort_end_date",
    cohortDate = "cohort_start_date"
  ) |>
  renameCohort("untreated")
cdm <- bind(cdm$treated, cdm$untreated, name = "states")

# Model first discontinuation: untreated is an absorbing state.
# Matrix state names must match the cohort names.
trans <- transMat(
  x = list(2, integer()),
  names = c("treated", "untreated")
)

# Estimate probabilities during the first year, overall and by initial state.
result <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(
  cohort = cdm$states,
  trans = trans,
  followUpDays = 365,
  stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated")
)
tidy(result) |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 10
#>   cdm_name initial_state variable_name  variable_level probability
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <chr>          <chr>                <dbl>
#> 1 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   0                    1    
#> 2 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 0                    0    
#> 3 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   15                   0.320
#> 4 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 15                   0.680
#> 5 GiBleed  overall       prob_treated   16                   0.319
#> 6 GiBleed  overall       prob_untreated 16                   0.681
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: cohort_table_name <chr>, follow_up_days <chr>,
#> #   state_hierarchy <chr>, state_step <chr>, transitions <chr>

# Sex is constant within each person and can be used for stratification.
cdm$states <- PatientProfiles::addSex(cdm$states)
bySex <- summariseMultistateProbabilities(
  cohort = cdm$states,
  trans = trans,
  strata = list("sex"),
  followUpDays = 365,
  stateHierarchy = c("treated", "untreated")
)
#> `cohort_table_name` eliminated from settings as all elements are NA.
bySex |>
  filterGroup(initial_state == "treated") |>
  filterStrata(sex == "Female") |>
  tidy() |>
  head()
#> # A tibble: 6 × 10
#>   cdm_name initial_state sex    variable_name  variable_level probability
#>   <chr>    <chr>         <chr>  <chr>          <chr>                <dbl>
#> 1 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   0                    1    
#> 2 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 0                    0    
#> 3 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   15                   0.305
#> 4 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 15                   0.695
#> 5 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_treated   22                   0.208
#> 6 GiBleed  treated       Female prob_untreated 22                   0.792
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: follow_up_days <chr>, state_hierarchy <chr>,
#> #   state_step <chr>, transitions <chr>

cdmDisconnect(cdm)
